about: Values the game needs that are not in the NASA/paper-sourced JSON files. Every entry carries a status: verified (from the listed source), derived (computed from sourced data with a stated method), estimate (secondary source, unconfirmed), or game_defined (chosen for gameplay). All game_defined values are listed in README.md. Prepared with AI (Claude) assistance.

parking_orbit_alt_km.note: typical low parking orbit before the upper stage escape burn

budget_musd.note: Real OSIRIS-REx: about $800M mission (excluding launch) + $183.5M Atlas V 411 launch = $983.5M (real_mission.json). Rounded up to $1,000M so the real design fits with a thin margin.

challenges.source: mission_options.json (NASA/JPL trajectory selected for the challenge)

launch_vehicle_model.method: Payload capacity vs C3 is computed with the user-supplied equations: the upper stage must raise a payload from a circular parking orbit (v_circ = sqrt(mu/r), vis-viva with a = r) to the hyperbolic departure speed v = sqrt(C3 + v_esc^2), where v_esc = sqrt(2 mu / r) (escape velocity; vis-viva with a = -mu/C3). The required delta-v is then fed into the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation for the upper stage. The only free parameter (usable upper-stage propellant left in the parking orbit) is calibrated so each curve passes through one sourced data point.

stage_dry_kg.note: approximate Centaur III single-engine dry mass

calibration_point.note: NASA Launch Services Program data for Falcon 9 with drone-ship booster recovery (Mars, C3 4.3), as republished by Spaceflight101

falcon_heavy.upper_stage: Falcon Heavy second stage (Merlin Vacuum, RP-1/LOX)

calibration_point.note: NASA Launch Services Program data for Falcon Heavy with core recovery (Mars, C3 4.3), as republished by Spaceflight101

mass_kg.note: Chosen so the real OSIRIS-REx configuration (all instruments, large array, HGA, shield level 2) gives the real 880 kg dry mass (parts.json reference_spacecraft).

cost_musd.note: Bus + operations so the real configuration costs about $800M (real_mission.json).

power_w.note: Housekeeping load: avionics, heaters, reaction wheels.

ocams.note: 3 cameras x 0.6 kg and 5.3 W from a secondary site (parts.json note), unconfirmed.

tagsam.note: No sourced mass or power found (parts.json needs_source).

propulsion_options.name: Hydrazine monopropellant (as flown)
propulsion_options.fuel: hydrazine (N2H4), decomposed on a catalyst bed
propulsion_options.pros: Simple, restartable, precise. What OSIRIS-REx flew.
propulsion_options.cons: Lowest efficiency of the liquid options.

propulsion_options.name: Bipropellant MMH / NTO
propulsion_options.pros: Higher exhaust velocity: same delta-v with less propellant.
propulsion_options.cons: Heavier engines and plumbing, more expensive, more complex.

propulsion_options.name: Solid kick motor
propulsion_options.cons: Once lit it burns to depletion: no throttle, no restart. A sample return needs several burns.

propulsion_options.name: Hybrid motor
propulsion_options.pros: Can be shut down by closing the oxidizer valve; safer than solids.
propulsion_options.cons: Limited restarts and still heavier than monoprop for the same job.

proximity_ops.note: approach, orbit insertion, TAG rehearsals and back-away

return_departure.note: set close to OSIRIS-REx's May 2021 Bennu departure burn

proximity_ops.note: real OSIRIS-REx stayed about 2.4 years (arrival 2018-12-03, departure May 2021)

return_cruise.note: real OSIRIS-REx return took about 2.4 years (sample landed 2023-09-24)

sample.label: Return at least 60 g of pristine carbon-rich regolith
